questions.q: Where do you go to create a new scoped application?
options: System Properties > New Scope
System Applications > Studio > Create Application
Service Catalog > New App Request
User Administration > Create Application
questions.explain: Studio, reached from System Applications, is the real entry point for creating and building scoped applications.

questions.q: What happens to the scope identifier once an application is created?
options: It cannot be changed, because it's baked into the real name of every table, field, and other scoped artifact created inside the app
It only matters for the first 24 hours after creation
It can be freely renamed at any time with no side effects
It automatically regenerates itself every time a new table is added
questions.explain: The identifier is woven into every table, field, and reference the moment they're created — not a safe or supported thing to change later.

questions.q: What does the Version field on a scoped application track?
options: The number of tables currently in the application
The application's lifecycle — relevant to publishing and distributing the app
The ServiceNow platform release the instance is running
The number of developers who have opened the app in Studio
questions.explain: Version supports application lifecycle and publishing/distribution, briefly mentioned as beyond this course's depth.

questions.q: What does creating a scoped application generate automatically?
options: A new ServiceNow instance
A new user account for the application owner
A duplicate of the Global scope
A new sys_scope record, plus that application's organized file structure in Studio
questions.explain: The sys_scope record and the application's file-structure container are both set up the moment the application is created.

questions.q: Why should scope naming convention be decided before clicking Create Application, not after?
options: Because naming conventions have no real impact on anything technical
Because the scope identifier that results from the name cannot be changed later without effectively rebuilding the application
Because Studio charges extra for renaming an application
Because the name field is read-only and pre-filled by ServiceNow
questions.explain: Since the identifier is permanent and structural, getting the naming convention wrong means starting over, not editing a field.
